titleStmt.title: Close of the Geneva forecast for 1533, with colophon and motto

respStmt.resp: Working transcription and translation, prepared with AI assistance
respStmt.name: Brelochs project

sourceDesc.bibl: Anton Brelochs, Practique ou pronostication nouvelle Dallemaigne, et almanach véritable, Geneva, Gabriel Pomar, [1532]. Bibliothèque de Genève, Bsa 46, GLN 5819. Facsimile, final printed leaf [A4]r, e-rara image [11].

editorialDecl.p: The six numbered lines begin at the pointing hand below the December table. Abbreviations are expanded and long s is normalized. Spacing and punctuation are lightly regularized. The leaf has surface damage through the middle. The reading of the damaged portions, including the verb of prayer and the colophon, follows comparison with Antal Lökkös, Pronostication inconnue dans la reliure d’un missel, Genava n.s. 33 (1985), 65–74, at 74. Unusual spellings are retained. The English renders the sense of the six lines in three groups.

div.p:
Et par ainsi se fine ma practique: prins dens naturelles
influences des constellations: pour l’aduisement des humains
Pour quoy nous prierons tous dieu deuotement: qu’il
nous veulle destourner tous inconueniens. Amen.
Translaté & Imprimé a Genesue par Gabriel Pomar

figure.figDesc: Two angels supporting the arms of Geneva beneath the motto.

div.p: And so ends my forecast, drawn from the natural influences of the constellations to give people warning. For this reason we shall all pray devoutly to God that he may turn every misfortune away from us. Amen.
Translated and printed at Geneva by Gabriel Pomar.
